text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- The chairmen of Centre Party and Leftist Alliance parliamentary groups Aapo Saari and Esko Helle to be challenged by rivalling candidates as parliament spring season opens today.
- Chairman of Metal Workers Union Per-Erik Lundh wants the next incomes settlement to bring moderate pay rises.
- Students seeking their "inner animal" study chimpanzee behaviour in Tampere. @
- Swedish Skanska's Finnish subsidiary Skanska Oy is winning significant construction projects in Russia and has a growing orderstock there, Skanska Oy managing director says.
- Finnish corporate bond market is almost non-existant. Cheap financing is available elsewhere and companies are unwilling to even try tapping the market, bankers say.
- Partek seeks to sell its concrete elements unit, its lorry manufacture unit and real estate, CEO Christoffer Taxell says. @

- Helsinki telephone company HPY plans to introduce time-based fees evenings and weekends to cut Internet surfers' "exceptionally long" telephone calls. Internet surfing at HPY's network alone doubled to 12 million minutes by December last year from a year earlier. @

- Elake-Varma managing director Paavo Pitkanen estimates work pension contributions will gradually increase as the population is ageing and there is no threat pensions would have to be lowered this decade.
